**WorldView 3 Mosaicking, and Cloud Masking**

This script mosaics multiple WorldView-3 satellite scenes into a single image and applies cloud and shadow masking to prepare the data for further analysis.

The workflow begins by loading the required packages.

```{r}
#| label: Packages

library(terra)
library(sf)
library(reticulate) # provides an R interface to Python modules, classes, and functions.
library(RStoolbox)

```

WorldView-3 data are provided as a series of .tif files. In this workflow, multispectral images for each month are mosaicked into a single composite image, and panchromatic images for each month are similarly mosaicked into a single file. The WorldView-3 scenes, including both multispectral and panchromatic bands, are then imported into R for further processing.

```{r}
#| labbel: image-scenes

# set the working directory

setwd("C:/Users/cp844/University of Exeter/TESSLab - Chafika Phiri Data/Objective 3 Manuscript/Satellite Data")

# kremetart scenes with multispectral bands collected on July 22, 2024.

krem_ms_july_files <- list.files(
  "Data/050333425010_01_Kre/050333425010_01_P001_MUL",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

krem_pan_july_files <- list.files(
  "Data/050333425010_01_Kre/050333425010_01_P001_PAN",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

krem_ms_feb_files <- list.files(
  "Data/050333425010_01_Kre/050333425010_01_P002_MUL",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

krem_pan_feb_files <- list.files(
  "Data/050333425010_01_Kre/050333425010_01_P002_PAN",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

# mapungubwe scenes

maps_ms_july_files <- list.files("Data/050333425020_01_Maps/050333425020_01_P001_MUL",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

maps_pan_july_files <- list.files("/Data/050333425020_01_Maps/050333425020_01_P001_PAN",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

maps_ms_feb_files <- list.files("Data/050333425020_01_Maps/050333425020_01_P002_MUL",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

maps_pan_feb_files <- list.files("Data/050333425020_01_Maps/050333425020_01_P002_PAN",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

# Load each multispectral band as a list of SpatRaster objects

krem_ms_july_spatraster <- sprc(krem_ms_july_files)
krem_pan_july_spatraster <- sprc(krem_pan_july_files)
krem_ms_feb_spatraster <- sprc(krem_ms_feb_files)
krem_pan_feb_spatraster <- sprc(krem_pan_feb_files)
maps_ms_july_spatraster <- sprc(maps_ms_july_files)
maps_pan_july_spatraster <- sprc(maps_pan_july_files)
maps_ms_feb_spatraster <- sprc(maps_ms_feb_files)
maps_pan_feb_spatraster <- sprc(maps_pan_feb_files)

# mosaic the spatraster to generate a single image for each month and sensor

krem_ms_july_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(krem_ms_july_spatraster)
krem_pan_july_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(krem_pan_july_spatraster)
krem_ms_feb_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(krem_ms_feb_spatraster)
krem_pan_feb_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(krem_pan_feb_spatraster)
maps_ms_july_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(maps_ms_july_spatraster)
maps_pan_july_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(maps_pan_july_spatraster)
maps_ms_feb_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(maps_ms_feb_spatraster)
maps_pan_feb_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(maps_pan_feb_spatraster)

# save all the mosaicked images

writeRaster(krem_ms_july_mosaic, "Data/Merged/Kremetart/krem_ms_july_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(krem_pan_july_mosaic, "Data/Merged/Kremetart/krem_pan_july_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(krem_ms_feb_mosaic, "Data/Merged/Kremetart/krem_ms_feb_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(krem_pan_feb_mosaic, "Data/Merged/Kremetart/krem_pan_feb_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)


writeRaster(maps_ms_july_mosaic, "Data/Merged/Maps/maps_ms_july_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(maps_pan_july_mosaic, "Data/Merged/Maps/maps_pan_july_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(maps_ms_feb_mosaic, "Data/Merged/Maps/maps_ms_feb_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(maps_pan_feb_mosaic, "Data/Merged/Maps/maps_pan_feb_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

```

**Cloud and shadow masking**

Cloud and shadow masking is performed using the OmnicloudMask model. As the model is implemented in Python, the reticulate package is used to interface Python within the R environment.

The OmnicloudMask model was trained on Sentinel-2 imagery with a spatial resolution of 10 m. To ensure compatibility, the higher-resolution WorldView-3 imagery (0.3 m) is resampled to 10 m prior to inference.

```{python}

import rasterio as rio
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from omnicloudmask import predict_from_array

# Path to your image

img_path = "Data/Merged/Kremetart_WV3/krem_feb_pansharpened.tiff"

with rio.open(img_path) as src:
  
    # Read bands (7=NIR,5=Red,3=Green for example)
    
    img = src.read([7, 5, 3]).astype("float32")
    img /= 2047.0  

    mask = predict_from_array(img)

mask = np.squeeze(mask)

# Plot results

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 7))

axes[0].imshow(np.transpose(img, (1, 2, 0)))
axes[0].set_title("True Color Composite (NIR, Red, Green)")
axes[0].axis("off")

cmap = plt.cm.get_cmap('tab10', 4)
im = axes[1].imshow(mask, cmap=cmap, vmin=0, vmax=3)
axes[1].set_title("Cloud Mask")
axes[1].axis("off")
cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes[1], ticks=[0,1,2,3])
cbar.ax.set_yticklabels(['Clear', 'Shadow', 'Cloud', 'Other'])

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()


```

Overlay the cloud and shadow mask images on the RGB

```{python}

from pathlib import Path
import rasterio as rio
from rasterio.warp import reproject, Resampling
import numpy as np
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

from omnicloudmask import predict_from_array
import omnicloudmask

# Set resolution for OmniCloudMask

required_res = 10  

# Load WorldView-3 image

img_path = "Data/Merged/Kremetart_WV3/krem_feb_pansharpened.tiff"
src = rio.open(img_path)

# Ensure 8 bands are present

channel_count = src.meta["count"]
if channel_count == 8:
    print("Found all 8 channels")
    GRB_NIR_bands = [5, 3, 2, 8]  
else:
    raise ValueError("Image does not have 8 bands.")

# Resample to 10m resolution for prediction

res = src.res
RGBN_array = src.read(
    GRB_NIR_bands,
    out_shape=(
        4,
        int(src.height * res[0] / required_res),
        int(src.width * res[0] / required_res),
    ),
)

RGB_array = RGBN_array[:3].transpose(1, 2, 0)
RGN_array = RGBN_array[[0, 1, 3]]

# Predict cloud and shadow mask

mask = predict_from_array(RGN_array)

# Resample mask back to original resolution

mask_resized = np.empty((src.height, src.width), dtype=np.uint8)
reproject(
    source=mask[0].astype(np.uint8),
    destination=mask_resized,
    src_transform=rio.transform.from_bounds(*src.bounds, width=mask.shape[2], height=mask.shape[1]),
    dst_transform=src.transform,
    src_crs=src.crs,
    dst_crs=src.crs,
    resampling=Resampling.nearest
)

# Read all 8 bands at full resolution

full_image = src.read()  # shape: (8, H, W)

# Mask cloud/shadow pixels by setting them to 0

masked_image = full_image.copy()
masked_pixels = (mask_resized != 0)  
masked_image[:, masked_pixels] = 0

# Save masked image

masked_output_path = "Data/Merged/Kremetart_WV3/2026Kremetart_feb_Pansharped_Masked.tif"
meta = src.meta.copy()
meta.update({
    "driver": "GTiff",
    "dtype": "uint16",  # Adjust if your image uses a different type
    "count": 8
})

with rio.open(masked_output_path, "w", **meta) as dst:
    dst.write(masked_image)

print(f"Masked image with 8 bands saved to:\n{masked_output_path}")
 
```
